title: Holiday Jingle Bell Luncheon
description: Join us for great music, great company and great food while celebrating the holidays. Enjoy the familiar favourites of slow-roasted turkey with stuffing, potatoes and gravy, along with a fancy dessert and seasonal entertainment. This activity is not applicable to pay by Rec Credits.

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Charmaine Liu
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: Charmaine Liu.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Isaac Juarez-Flores
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: Isaac Juarez-Flores.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Modern: Primary Long-Term
description:
This Course is part of the Shadbolt's long-term progressive training program. Modern dance is distinguished by its use of expression, exploration and movement invention. This dance form focuses on dynamic alignment, use of gravity and momentum through the exploration of floor work and sequences that move three-dimensionally through space. Students explore the concepts of body, dynamics, shape and space to the sounds of live percussion music. The focus is on dance as an art form and students are given the tools to develop self-expression in a process oriented environment. Children must be in Grade 1 to register. Please note this class takes place on Saturday; other dates listed are rehearsal and performance days and are subject to change. Fee includes cost of accompanist. Extra fees for performance ($17.00), and costume ($30.00).

title: Jr Golf | Play (age 8-10) | Skills Development | 8 weeks
description:
A 8-week program designed for developing golfers with some experience. You’ll level up your putting, short game, full swing, and decision-making through fun competitive drills and games, with the goal of playing at the pitch and putt.
Golfers will be provided an environment where they will be supported in development of skills. The achievement of standards leading to confident on course experience.
Level: Beg/int and Intermediate
Number of Classes: 8
Class Duration: 90 mins each
Min/Max number of participants:6
Students are expected to bring their own clubs for this program
Classes are conducted in rain or shine
Class cancellation / refund policy: 7 days' notice is required for cancellation and refund.

description:

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Lana Djordan
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: Lana Djordan.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Creative Dance to Live Music
description:
Children are introduced to the joy of dance with live music in a supportive and creative environment. They learn the elements of dance, develop movement skills, respond creatively to movement suggestions, and develop musicality. Children must be the required age at the start of the first class. Cost includes accompanist fee. Please dress your child in comfortable clothing.
Instructor: Trevor Klushin.
REFUND POLICYYou'll receive a full refund if the activity is cancelled or if you request a refund at least 7 days before the start of the activity. If your request comes less than 7 days before the activity starts, there is a 10% refund fee on the original price you paid.
After the activity has started, refunds are pro-rated according to the number of sessions remaining and a 10% refund fee will be applied. No refunds will be granted after the third session has ended.
Note: There may be exceptions to these cancellation and refund guidelines as noted in the activity description. Please check your receipt.

Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

ageText: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs,

title: Cartooning
description: Students learn the fundamentals of drawing people, animals and props with an abundance of personality. Incorporate characters into a background to bring out the 'Zoom! Wow! Zing! and Whooosh!' of great visual story telling. Facial expressions, comic strips, animation flipbook-style drawn projects, interactive moving paper cartoon characters and dozens of other techniques are explored. Materials include pen and ink, watercolour, Sculpey and or Plasticine. No class Oct 10th. Instructor: Michael Allard
ageText: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 13 yrs,

Instructor: Jay Johnson
ageText: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 14 yrs,

title: Drawing & Painting
description: Students explore their own artistic language by learning colour theory, composition, texture, line and form. Working from observation and imagination, skills are developed using a wide variety of mediums such as acrylics, watercolour, oil and chalk pastels, charcoal, ink, collage and mixed-media. All supplies included. No experience necessary. No class Oct 10th. Instructor: Michael Allard
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs,

title: Drawing, Painting & Sculpture
description: Students take part in a variety of 2 & 3 dimensional projects with an emphasis on creative exploration, observation, manual dexterity and playfulness. Instructor: Cherry Lu
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs,

title: Video
description: A dynamic and collaborative learning environment where students create a short film based on a story generated in class. ageText: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

ageText: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 6 yrs,

A supply fee of $5.00 is included in the fee.

title: Martial Gym for Functional Fitness
description: Rather than memorizing sequences of exercises, exercisers are taught simple goals/guidelines to create their own exercise routine that is relevant and effective. Classes are tailored specifically to seniors, to protect as well as have fun. The goal is to empower seniors through improved flexibility, balance, co-ordination, strength and knowledge. With new movement patterns for fitness and a new understanding of how to effectively neutralize hazards, seniors are better equipped to maintain their quality of life for longer. Frequent interaction and feedback are used to improve quality of movement and understanding. Martial Gym taps into gymnastics for fun and variety and ancient Chinese secrets for health and effectiveness. Drawing on aspects of both martial arts and rhythmic gymnastics, learn to stimulate your body and mind's adaptability to different situations. Using light objects, games, music and interaction with other participants, progress beyond mirroring an instructor's movements to improving your own balance, strength, coordination and self-defence skills. Participants must be able to get down onto a mat on the floor and back up again, in order to participate in this class.

title: Blossoming Artists
description: Children are given the opportunity to thrive by developing and building upon their innate artistic instincts and imagination. Instructors provide guidance and encouragement with fun projects and tons of different art materials to explore. Our goal is to build creative skills and confidence so that children feel comfortable to take risks in their art making. No Class Oct 11th. Instructor: Polly Faminow
ageText: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs,

title: Blossoming Artists
description: Children are given the opportunity to thrive by developing and building upon their innate artistic instincts and imagination. ageText: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs,

title: Drawing, Painting & Collage
description: Explore, Imagine & Create! Students develop artistic expression and skill through drawing, painting and collage making techniques (Pop-ups and layering in 2 and 3D). Experiment with a variety of materials - pencils, felts, pastels, watercolour & tempera paint, collage materials and papers - while learning about colour ,texture, composition. A supportive and engaging environment that encourages self-expression, problem solving, confidence building and FUN! No class Oct 11th. Instructor: Mat Holmstrom
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs,

title: Drawing, Painting & Sculpture
description: Students take part in a variety of 2 & 3 dimensional projects with an emphasis on creative exploration, observation, manual dexterity and playfulness. Colour, composition and mark making are introduced with drawing and painting materials and building skills are developed with simple sculptures. $5 supply fee applicable. No class Oct 11th. Instructor: Mat Holmstrom
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs,

title: Artist's Studio for Teens
description: Longer session, 10 weeks of art making! Open studio opportunity to explore and develop your own artistic interest, practice, and portfolio through drawing, painting, sculpture, and or mix media. Each week, the instructor will introduce a short lesson, from colour theory to art history to contemporary concepts, to build artistic repertoire. Individual feedback, support and tailored materials will be provided for each young artist to support individual development. Artist quality supplies provided. $15.00 visual arts material fee. Instructor: Cherry Lu
ageText: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs,

title: Teen Drawing
description: Investigate technical aspects of drawing and work on specific projects designed to challenge and inspire. Develop your abilities with graphite, pencil crayons, pen and ink, pastels and other dry media. All levels welcome and students work at their own pace. The goal is to get you to your next level through consistent practice. $10.00 visual arts material fee for Sketchbook is applicable. No class Oct 11. Instructor: Christy Dunsmore
ageText: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs,

title: Teen Painting
description: Students explore painting techniques and materials, especially designed to develop creative ability through a blend of instruction, freedom of expression and individual attention. Wear clothes that are suitable for art activities. $10.00 extra visual arts material fee applicable. No class Oct 11. Instructor: Christy Dunsmore
ageText: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs,

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term - Victor T. (Sat)
description:
In these private piano lessons, beginners to advanced students learn at their own pace. These private lessons are tailored to the expectations of the student while at the same time learning theory, ear training and receiving technical assistance. If two people from the same family wish to take a lesson together, please register one family member to hold the spot and then contact the programmer. They will change the class to semi-private and facilitate the change of registration. Students must have a keyboard at home with full size weighted keys. A piano is supplied for in-class use. Instructor: Victor Tang.
Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program.

It's one step at a time- while having fun!Learn about musicality, balance, co-ordination, memory and styling techniques. Get started dancing today and meet friendly people sharing the same interest in dance!
Please wear comfortable, smooth sole shoes to allow for easy dance movements.
There is a possibility that a dancer will be moved to an alternate session if it is deemed that they are not registered in the correct level. No transfers will occur after the third class.

title: Acrylic with Brush & Palette Knife
description:
Join our acrylic painting class, led by an experienced art teacher Irina, where you'll explore acrylic technique and unleash your creativity. Whether you are a beginner or intermediate student, this class offers personalized guidance to help you master the art of acrylic painting using traditional paint brush. Learn how to blend colours, create texture, and develop your unique style in a friendly and supportive environment.
Irina will also guide you through an immersive journey of palette knife painting- where every stroke tells a story and every canvas becomes a masterpiece! Palette knife painting is a technique in which an artist uses a palette knife instead of a traditional brush to apply paint to a canvas. In this form, you will apply thick layers of paint directly onto the canvas, creating textured and dynamic surfaces. This technique allows for a more expressive and gestural style, with bold strokes and distinct marks.
A $20 Supply Fee is included in the displayed price to help cover the cost of supplies used during the class.

If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

description:

title: Comics & Cartooning
description:
Students study different styles from cartoons and popular media to learn what makes an effective cartoon character. They focus on character dynamics and how to convey effective characters through shapes and structure. Looking at different types of characters and body types, they learn to think outside the box from what they would normally draw.
Instructor: Vanessa Kelly

title: I Can Make a Story
description:
If you give a kid a pencil, they might create something amazing! In this story writing class, kids will learn how their favourite books, movies, and TV shows are created, with lessons about different storytelling elements. Students will learn how to create characters, describe setting, and construct a compelling plot with a variety of writing- and art-based activities. While activities will involve independent reading & writing, children can also expect to draw & colour, listen to read-alouds, and engage in creative story games. If your child loves storytelling (in all its forms), then I Can Make a Story is the class for them!
Instructor: Mackenzie Sewell.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs,

title: Storybuilding
description:
Does your child love fantasy stories? Are they crazy about science fiction? Do they love creating their own worlds, full of magic, fascinating creatures, or impossible technology? In Storybuilding, students learn story-writing techniques specific to the genres of fantasy and science fiction, such as worldbuilding, creating magic systems, inventing languages, and so much more. Students will apply what they learn by writing their own fantasy/science fiction stories! While most of our activities will involve reading & writing, kids can also expect to practice their drawing skills, listen to read alouds, and engage in creative story games. Flex your child’s imagination with Storybuilding!

Instructor: Mackenzie Sewell.

title: Watercolour Wonders
description:
Join us for a fun-filled adventure in our Watercolor Wonders class designed especially for creative kids aged 6-7! In this exciting class, young artists will explore the magical world of watercolor painting. Through playful activities, they'll learn basic techniques like blending, lifting, and layering colors while experimenting with different brushes and papers.
Each week, we'll focus on a new theme, from vibrant landscapes to whimsical creatures, allowing children to express their imagination and build confidence in their artistic skills. With plenty of encouragement and guidance, every child will create their very own masterpiece to take home!Get ready to splash some color, make new friends, and discover the joy of painting in a fun, supportive environment! All materials are provided. Just bring your creativity and a big smile!
Instructor: Tami Murray
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs,

title: Drawing & Painting: Portraiture & Still Life
description:
Unleash your artistic potential in our engaging Drawing & Painting: Portraiture and Still Life class! This course is perfect for budding artists looking to refine their skills while exploring two fundamental aspects of art.
In the portraiture segment, students will learn techniques for capturing likeness and expression, using a variety of mediums. Through guided exercises and individual projects, participants will develop their understanding of proportions, shading, and the unique features that make each person special.
The still life portion of the course focuses on composition, color theory, and the interplay of light and shadow. Students will arrange their own still life setups, experimenting with different materials and styles to create striking, personal works of art.
Join us for an inspiring journey into the world of portrait and still life art, and leave with your own stunning creations! All materials are included.
Instructor: Tami Murray

title: Drawing & Cartooning
description: Longer session for 10 weeks of art Fun! Students learn the fundamentals of drawing people, animals and props with an abundance of personality. Incorporate characters into a background to bring out the 'Zoom! Wow! Zing! 'Whooosh!' of great visual story telling. Facial expressions, comic strips, animation flipbook-style drawn projects, interactive moving paper cartoon characters and dozens of other techniques are explored. Materials include pen and ink, watercolour, Sculpey and or Plasticine. No class Oct 12. Instructor: Michael Allard

title: Belly Dance: Beginner
description:
This fun class will introduce you to one of the oldest forms of dance. Learn how to isolate specific body parts and muscle groups and transition into basic dance movements, all set to traditional ethnic music focusing on Egyptian techniques. Learn how to shimmy like the pros! No experience necessary.
It is recommended that students wear comfortable clothes to workout/dance in. This class does not require special shoes as it is primarily taught bare foot or in socks but if you require orthotics, soft flat dance shoes such as jazz shoes or ballet practice shoes are recommended. Students are also requested to bring a scarf or something to tie around their hips and their own water bottle. Students are also welcome to bring a small notebook if they choose but not required.
Instructor: Melody

title: Musical Theatre Ensemble: Junior
description:
Sing, Dance, Act. Tell a story.
In this fun and intensive program, young performers will be guided through the creation of two narrative driven public performances featuring complete plotlines, character development, and integrated choreography.
Taught by professional performing artists and accompanied by live music, the Junior Ensemble learns about basic singing techniques, creative expression and basic rhythms. There is a focus on creative play and an exploration of how stories are created and developed in this discipline.
The fall session is spent working towards an in-studio performance of an original musical revue in the style of the classic Holiday Special of stage and screen.
In collaboration with the senior ensemble, the winter and spring sessions develop and rehearse a full-length musical show, to be performed in the Shadbolt Centre’s Studio Theatre, incorporating rehearsed lighting, staging and sound design by our professional technical staff.
Bringing stories to life and bringing people together.
Instructors: Illya Mulji & Evelyn Evelyn Dlouhy
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a year long commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are NOT permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program.
Payment Plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of paymentdue at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

description: Therapeutic Yoga is a gentle, holistic, & functional approach to overall well-being, designed for all levels. Through this practice, you will learn to use props, breathing, asana postures, & mindfullness techniques therapeutically. It is fully adaptable to your unique physical, mind, & emotional needs. title: Communicating with Confidence: Reading the Room
description:
You have great ideas, but getting them to land clearly feels daunting. Communicating with Confidence is a hands-on, low-pressure workshop series designed to take the stress out of public speaking, communication, and presentations.
Across three standalone sessions, we explore the core elements of communication: Yourself, Your Audience, and Your Content. This session focuses on your audience and reading the room.
Communicating your thoughts and ideas doesn’t have to feel like a stressful performance; it can feel like a normal conversation. This workshop takes the pressure off you by shifting your focus outward. We’ll explore the real-world dynamics of human connection, look at the factors that affect how we communicate, and practice tools to adapt when a room feels cold. Through collaborative exercises, you’ll learn how to build a genuine, comfortable bridge with your listeners.
Each workshop stands entirely on its own, so you can register for just one or explore all three to build your complete toolkit.
Discover the other workshops here:
Oct 21 Showing Up
Dec 9 Organizing your Thoughts
Offered by Instructor Amanada Haggett and The Imagination Forge

title: Communicating with Confidence: Organizing your thoughts
description:
You have great ideas, but getting them to land clearly feels daunting. Communicating with Confidence is a hands-on, low-pressure workshop series designed to take the stress out of public speaking, communication, and presentations.
Across three standalone sessions, we explore the core elements of communication: Yourself, Your Audience, and Your Content. This session focuses on what you're saying and how you say it.
Knowing what you want to say is one thing; getting it out of your head clearly is another. If your brain tends to spin with too many ideas or facts when you're put on the spot, this session is for you. We’ll look at how to structure your thoughts so they make sense to different kinds of communicators, practice weaving a narrative into your content, and clarify exactly why you are sharing your ideas. To tie it all together, you'll build a short presentation in a highly supportive environment and get comfortable handling questions.
Each workshop stands entirely on its own, so you can register for just one or explore all three to build your complete toolkit.

title: Professional Practices for Emerging Artists
description: Whether you are preparing for your first exhibition or looking to develop a more focused artistic practice, this introductory course provides practical tools for navigating the contemporary art world. Through a combination of studio work, discussion, critique, and hands-on exercises, students will develop a small, cohesive body of work while learning how to present themselves and their artwork professionally. Topics include developing an artistic voice, building a portfolio, writing artist statements and biographies, documenting artwork, preparing exhibition submissions, and applying to artist calls, grants, and residency opportunities. Students will leave the course with the beginnings of a professional portfolio package and a stronger understanding of how to share their work with the broader arts community. No Class Oct 12. Libby Adams is a Certified Travel Counsellor with Journeys By Libby (affiliated with Nexion Canada, ULC), specializing in helping travellers 50+ and their families turn their travel dreams into comfortable, well-planned experiences.

title: Martial Gym for Functional Fitness
description: Rather than memorizing sequences of exercises, exercisers are taught simple goals/guidelines to create their own exercise routine that is relevant and effective. Classes are tailored specifically to seniors, to protect as well as have fun. The goal is to empower seniors through improved flexibility, balance, co-ordination, strength and knowledge. With new movement patterns for fitness and a new understanding of how to effectively neutralize hazards, seniors are better equipped to maintain their quality of life for longer. Frequent interaction and feedback are used to improve quality of movement and understanding. Martial Gym taps into gymnastics for fun and variety and ancient Chinese secrets for health and effectiveness. Drawing on aspects of both martial arts and rhythmic gymnastics, learn to stimulate your body and mind's adaptability to different situations. Using light objects, games, music and interaction with other participants, progress beyond mirroring an instructor's movements to improving your own balance, strength, coordination and self-defence skills. Participants must be able to get down onto a mat on the floor and back up again, in order to participate in this class.

title: Ceramics 2: Refining Handbuilding
description: Slow precision describes the process and possibilities of handbuilding with clay. This new course offers intermediate and advanced techniques for working on larger and more complex ceramic forms. You will learn to create templates and simple bisque molds, and develop strategies for adding lids and handles to your work. Projects include a curved-sided box, large coiled vessels, and a kurinuki (carved) tray. Clay is not included in course fee. Students must purchase clay ticket from Front Office. Prerequisite: Ceramics 1: Introduction or Handbuilt Sculptural Techniques, or equivalent experience. Students must have some proficiency with basic handbuilding, including rolling coils and slabs. This course is not suitable for beginners. No class September 30 or November 11. Instructor: Fredi Rahn

title: Ceramics 3: Design With Crystalline
description: Create beautiful heirloom gifts, sculptures and ornaments finished with unique crystalline glazes. In this course you will learn suitable forms and catchers for crystalline glazes, and proper glaze application. The last week of class includes a group critique of the results and removal of the catchers. This advanced-level course is not suitable for beginners. Participants must be capable of centring clay on a wheel and throwing complex forms. If a patron does not have the required wheel throwing experience, they may be asked to withdraw. Please note that only pieces made during class will be fired with crystalline glazes, no externally produced ceramics from other studios or Open Workshops. Clay not included in course fee. C-3, C-4 and C-5 clay may be used in this class. The instructor will provide additional information about suitable clays. No refunds after September 14. No class October 27. title: Ceramics 3: From The Ashes
description: In this advanced specialty course, ceramic artist Cheryl Stapleton will lead participants through designing and preparing pots for sawdust, loading and firing the kiln, and then unloading and polishing the final pieces. Participants will form pots by hand or on the wheel, then burnish or apply terra sigillata to the surfaces. After bisque, the pots will be loaded and fired in the sawdust kiln with organic materials to create soft variations of colour on the surfaces of the works. Over 5 sessions, participants will complete 1 sawdust firing. Tools and clay not included in course fee. Students must purchase C-3 clay ticket from Front Office prior to start of class. This course is not suitable for beginners. No refunds after October 20. Mandatory attendance for the loading and unloading dates. The loading and firing of the sawdust kiln will happen on November 24. The kiln unload will happen on December 1.

description: Learn pottery, sculpture and ceramic arts in our professionally equipped studio. This course will cover wheel throwing and handbuilding techniques with a focus on creating works for a group raku firing on the final day of class. After being introduced to various building techniques, students are encouraged to explore their own ideas through individual projects. Returning students welcome. Raku is a traditional Japanese firing technique that involves removing glazed pots from a hot kiln and rapidly cooling them through combustion with sawdust and exposure to open air and water. The final result is brilliant metallic and white crackle surfaces. Supplies and firings included in the course fee. Students should wear old clothing to class. title: Ceramics: 2027 Wood Firing Reservation
description:
This is an expression of interest for ceramic artists, potters and sculptors to participate in wood firings in 2027 (March, April, October). Registration will be determined by reservation list. The first 38 registrants will be offered 3 cubic feet in one of the firings in 2027. When registration is complete, the Ceramic Arts Programmer will contact registrants by phone to confirm firing dates. Waitlistees will be added to the reservation list in order of registration. Registrants may request to have their name added to the reservation list for a second firing, but priority may be given to those not already confirmed to participate in another wood firing. To have your name added to the reservation list after November 1, 2026, please contact the Ceramic Arts Programmer at 604-205-3012.
Wood firing workshops are not suitable for beginners. All participants must have ceramic proficiency to bring 3 cubic feet of bisqueware in a range of different sizes. At least 1 cubic feet must be forms that are 8 inches or taller. Wood firings require participation in wood preparation and stoking. The cost of wood firing is $357.47 + tax, subject to change. The wood firing workshop includes glazing and wadding. Activity schedule:Wednesday: Measuring, Glazing & Wadding Shifts, 10am-2pm or 2:30-6:30pm (mandatory)Thursday: Kiln Loading Shifts, times variable (2-hour shift mandatory)Friday-Saturday: Firing, times variable (6-hour shift mandatory)Wednesday: Unloading & Shelf Grinding, 1:30-5:30pm (mandatory)

description:

title: Ceramics Alternative Firing: Raku
description: Western raku is a low-temperature, fast-firing process for finishing your ceramic sculptures with dazzling effects. Traditional and contemporary raku glazes such as white crackle and metallic copper are provided. Bring 3-4 bisque-fired pieces that can each individually fit within a box measuring 6 inches squared. You may bring additional pieces in case there is extra room in the kiln. Work should be made with a sculpture clay or a grey clay with grog. Glazes included, bring your own brushes. Wear close-toed shoes and wool, cotton or linen long-sleeved clothing. Participants will glaze their work from 10am-12pm, followed by the firing. Participants are responsible for ensuring they have enough work prepared in advance of the firing date. No refunds after November 14. Instructor: Tony WilsonSchedule:Glazing (2 hours) 10am-12pmFiring (4 hours) 12-4pm

title: Compound Lifting - Part 2: Bench Press & Overhead Press
description:
Learn the fundamentals of compound lifting and see the benefits! This three-part training program focuses on learning, practicing, and mastering the big 6 compound exercises (squats, deadlifts, bench press, overhead press, bent over row and pull ups). Learn the correct muscle groups to use, proper form, and modifications for each exercise. By training multiple muscle groups at once you will burn calories, improve intramuscular connection, core strength, balance, functional strength, muscular strength, and build more muscle mass along the way.
This is part 2 of a three-part compound lifting program. This session focuses on bench press and overhead shoulder press. Knowing the correct form is essential for feeling more comfortable in the gym. If you’ve ever asked yourself; where should the bar hit my chest in a bench press? Where should I place my hands on the bar? Should I arch my back or keep it flat? This is the class for you! Our knowledgeable instructor will guide you through how to move properly through both a bench press and overhead press while providing helpful tips and guidance along the way to ensure you are confident about each exercise.
Completion of the PAR-Q+ form is required to participate. Please see details below.

title: Reserve in Advance: Weight Room Orientation
description:
“Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.”

The goal of the weight room orientation is to provide someone new to exercise or new to the facility a basic introduction to the weight room.

  • A 45 minute safety weight room orientation. Participants will receive training on: safe practices in the weight room, proper use of equipment and a review of policies and etiquette.
  • We will provide you with the basics of how to use weight and cardio equipment. You will learn how to start, stop and change settings on cardio machines, change seat height and weight selections on machines, and have a discussion of proper form on the weight machines.
  • All instructors are experienced and certified.
  • NOTE: an orientation is NOT a personal training session.
  • Schedules are subject to change.

title: Watercolour Painting
description:
Watercolour has a unique and luminous charm unlike any other media. Painters are introduced to an enjoyable, loose, relaxed method of watercolour painting. Paints, brushes, papers, spray bottles, liquid frisket and their applications are introduced. Different methods of applying watercolour. flat and graded washes, wet-in-wet, dry-brush and spraying are explored. Basic principles such as composition, developing the focal point, atmospheric perspective and color mixing are covered. For everyone from complete beginner to intermediate level. Supply list will be provided prior to class start date.
Instructor: Irina Samarukava

Children learn basic handbuilding techniques such as slab work, coiling and wedging. The process of firing, then painting or glazing completes each creation. Supplies included in course fee. No class on October 12. Instructor: Allysha Hurd
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs,

title: Teen Handbuilding
description: This is a satellite program operated by the ceramics staff at the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, City of Burnaby's internationally renown ceramic arts facility. Learn ceramic arts in our purpose-built clay studio. This course will cover functional and sculptural handbuilding, and working with underglazes to create vibrant surfaces. After being introduced to various building techniques, students are encouraged to explore their own ideas through individual projects. Returning students welcome. Clay and supplies included in the course fee. Students should wear old clothing. No class October 12. Instructor: Eris Fitz-James
ageText: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 19 yrs,

title: Ceramics 1: Handbuilding
description:
This is a satellite program operated by the ceramics staff at the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, City of Burnaby's internationally renown ceramic arts facility. Try pottery in a purpose-built clay studio! You will learn several foundational handbuilding methods such as slabs, coils and pinching to create functional and sculptural works. You will also learn surface decoration techniques using underglaze. Clay and supplies included in course fee. No class October 13. Instructor: Allysha Hurd
Please note that participants will be eligible to register for Ceramics: Open Workshop for Current Students on Tuesdays from 1-3pm to practice their skills outside of regular class time. The instructor will share Open Workshop registration details during the first class.

title: I Can Make a Story
description:
If you give a kid a pencil, they might create something amazing! In this story writing class, kids will learn how their favourite books, movies, and TV shows are created, with lessons about different storytelling elements. Students will learn how to create characters, describe setting, and construct a compelling plot with a variety of writing- and art-based activities. title: Blades 1
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Blades skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. In this level, children learn about safety on the ice, how to fall down and stand up, walk on the ice without assistance and are introduced to stopping, gliding and sculling. By the end of this level children need to be able to skate the width of the rink with confidence using both feet along with demonstrating other building blocks. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Acro Dance 2 Long-Term
description:
A combination of dance and gymnastics. Children learn balances, the beginning elements of gymnastics and the basic steps of dance. These are put together to music, and the children learn a routine. title: Haunted History Walking Tour
description:
Join Burnaby Village Museum this October to learn all about seemingly haunted happenings in Deer Lake Park. From the stories of the former Oakalla Prison, to strange activities at Ceperley House, and unexplained events at our very own Burnaby Village Museum site, there is no shortage of spooky stories in the area.
This two-hour walking tour begins at the Burnaby Village Museum's main entrance, takes participants through the museum to the neighbouring Shadbolt Centre and Burnaby Art Gallery, where they will hear stories of suspicious circumstances and mysterious histories present at the various sites. Please note that entrance to the Burnaby Art Gallery and Shadbolt Centre are not included in this tour. Walking tours will take place rain or shine, please dress accordingly.
Age 16+.

title: Cottage Cheese Making Workshop
description:
Learn how to make fresh, creamy cottage cheese from scratch in this hands on, beginner friendly workshop. Working in small groups, you’ll heat, curdle, and strain your own batch of cottage cheese while learning the simple dairy science behind curds and whey. We’ll explore how to adjust texture, how to use different acids, and how to turn everyday milk into something special. While your curds drain, your instructor will prepare a warm cottage cheese pasta dish for the class to enjoy at the end. You’ll top it with your freshly made cottage cheese for a cozy, delicious tasting that shows just how versatile homemade cheese can be.

Just bring a tupperware container or jar to take your fresh cottage cheese home in.

title: Foundations of Bookbinding: Coptic Stitch
description:
In this hands-on course, participants will explore a stitching style with a bold, open aesthetic over the course of two 2-hour workshop sessions. The Coptic stitch, developed by early bookbinders, produces journals that lie completely flat and feature an elegantly exposed spine, ideal for sketching and showcasing decorative thread work.
Over the course of the workshop, participants will be guided through material preparation and the signature chain-like sewing pattern that makes this method so distinctive. There’s no prior experience needed from participants, just curiosity and a willingness to try something new.
The result? A durable, handmade journal that blends utility with visual flair, and a new technique participants can adapt for future creative projects. This is bookbinding at its most eye-catching and adaptable, perfect for anyone ready to experiment with craft and design.

title: Still Life Drawing & Painting: Acrylic or Oil
description:
This studio course develops drawing and painting skills by working from life. Students strengthen visual perception by learning to translate real objects into structured compositions. Foundational drawing skills, including proportion, value, and spatial relationships, are covered as the basis for painting. Students learn to organize canvas space through strong composition and to simplify forms into clear shapes, color masses, and light patterns.

Instruction then focuses on acrylic or oil painting techniques such as brush handling, paint application, layering, and edge control. Emphasis is placed on understanding paint behavior and using it expressively to build form, light, and atmosphere. By the end of the course, students will be able to create well-composed still life paintings from life; Students are encouraged to bring objects from home to add meaning and individuality.

title: Bronze Medallion
description: Prerequisites: Must be 13 years old OR have Bronze Star. Understand the lifesaving principles embodied in the four components of water rescue education: judgment, knowledge, skill and fitness. Rescuers learn self rescue techniques, defence and release methods, and tows and carries in preparation for challenging rescues involving conscious and unconscious victims of various types, including spinal injuries and circulatory emergencies. Lifesavers develop stroke efficiency and endurance in a timed swim. Includes the CPR-A certification. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: National Lifeguard Pool
description:
The NL Pool certification is designed to develop the fundamental values, judgment, knowledge, skills and fitness required by lifeguards. This course emphasizes the lifeguarding skills, principles and practices, and the decision-making processes that assist the lifeguard in providing effective safety supervision in swimming pool environments. Prerequisite: Bronze Cross (does not need to be current) and Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care (current award recommended) by the first day of the NL course. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Must be 15 years old by the last day of the course. Alert Manual is required and not included in fee. There is a non-refundable exam fee.
Students must be prepared to bring bathing suit, manual and paper for each class. Candidates will need to provide proof of the prerequisites on the 1st day of the course to the instructor or be sent home with no refund. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Recognized Agencies for Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care are: any Canadian branch of the Lifesaving Society, Canadian Red Cross, St John Ambulance, Canadian Heart and Stroke Foundation or Canadian Ski Patrol. 100% attendance is required.

title: Bronze Star
description: Prerequisites: Canadian Swim Patrol recommended and an ability to swim in deep water. Provides excellent preparation for success in obtaining the Bronze Medallion award. Develop problem solving and decision-making skills as they relate to water rescue and first aid as well as Water Smart confidence and the lifesaving skills needed to be one's own personal lifeguard. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.
ageText: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs,

title: Bronze Cross
description: Prerequisite: Bronze Medallion. Designed for lifesavers who want the challenge of more advanced training, including an introduction to safety supervision in aquatic facilities. Swimmers develop proficiency at performing patient assessments, managing aquatic spinal injuries and preventing loss of life in a variety of aquatic emergencies, while developing stroke endurance and fitness training skills. Includes the CPR-C certification and is one of the prerequisite awards for all advanced Lifeguarding and Leadership training programs. It is also worth two Grade 11 high school credits. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: Reserve In Advance: Recreational Hockey
description:
Get a great workout with a casual game of hockey. CSA-approved helmet with face mask or visor and hockey gloves are mandatory. Full hockey gear is recommended. No-check rules apply. Goalies must wear full gear. Not supervised.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Reserve in Advance: Figure Skating
description:
Practice the sport of Figure Skating at this drop-in. Participants must wear figure skates and confidently skate at Star 2+ (backwards cross over, 3-turns, toeloop, back spin). Skaters must have their own skates. (Recreational skates are not appropriate).
Reserved spots will be forfeited 10 minutes after the program has started. Check in at the front counter and pay prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist. Participants must have their own equipment.
Coaching is not permitted

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Reserve In Advance: Recreational Hockey
description:
Full hockey equipment and a CSA-approved helmet with face mask or visor and hockey gloves are strongly recommended. Games are not supervised and no-check rule apply. Reserve in advance online or drop-in if spots are available. 2 days in advance for Burnaby residents. 1 day in advance for non-Burnaby residents.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Dungeons & Dragons Adult Program - One Day
description:
For all those fans of D&D you can have even more fun as a family!!

Embark on a thrilling journey into the realm of imagination with our Dungeons & Dragons Program! This course offers an immersive and interactive experience in the world's greatest tabletop role-playing game.

In our program, participants will delve into the captivating universe of Dungeons & Dragons, where they will create their own heroes, forge friendships, and conquer challenges together. Led by experienced Dungeon Masters (DMs), our sessions blend storytelling, strategy, and teamwork to ignite the imagination and foster creative thinking.

title: Reserve In Advance: Adult Basketball
description:
Please arrive early and check in with staff at the gymnasium to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

Pre-requisite: Blades 2 or an evaluation. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase punch card on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs,

title: Reserve In Advance: Adult Badminton
description:
Please arrive early and check in with staff at the gymnasium to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Please arrive early and check in with staff at the gymnasium to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Blades 5
description: At this intermediate level children learn forward circle thrusts, walking crossovers, two-foot turns and continue to work on their edges and backward one-foot gliding. Prerequisite: Blades 4 or an evaluation. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Piano or Cello: Private Lesson Long-Term Joyce Wang
description:
Private piano lessons from September to June for students who have taken one or two terms of piano lessons already. Instructor: Joyce Wang.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Creative Writing through Tarot
description:
Discover a transformative approach to creative writing that dives deep into the unconscious and trusting your inner voice, using the rich symbolism of Tarot and archetypes.
A central focus of this approach is cultivating intuition as a creative tool—encouraging students to move beyond logic and let symbolic thinking, gut feeling, and imaginative play lead the way. Tarot becomes more than a writing prompt; it becomes a mirror of the psyche, helping students decode internal signals and follow narrative threads that may otherwise remain hidden.
This course offers practical tools to blend psychology, myth, and creativity.
All levels of writers welcome. Or even if you're not a writer, you may have a passion for Tarot and intuition development! You may take the course to help your creative process, or you may approach it as a self-help course that involves unlocking your unconscious, intuition, and personal narratives. If you have taken the course before, we will be delving a little deeper this time and it will be approached a bit differently.
Key Highlights:• Learn the basics of Tarot and how to read them• Use Tarot cards as prompts for character development and story arcs• Explore archetypes like the Hero, Shadow, and Trickster • Develop intuition and accessing the unconscious story material• Foster emotional authenticity and symbolic fluency through guided exercises• Cultivate personal insight, self-trust, and creative confidence
Renu Parmar is an experienced psychotherapist and writer. She is the author of The Colour of Snow, which won finalist - best fiction from the Independent Authors Network in 2020.

title: Ceramics: Open Workshop
description: Open Workshop spaces are available to individuals with some pottery and ceramics experience to work on and practice ceramic art. Patrons are limited to registering for a maximum of two Open Workshops per week (Monday-Sunday) and will be withdrawn from Open Workshops that exceed the maximum limit.

description:

- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details.- Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Reserve In Advance: Adult Badminton
description:
Please arrive early and check in with staff at the gymnasium to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Please arrive early and check in at the front counter to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Drum: Private Lesson Long-Term Allan Dionne
description:
Students can sign up for private drum set lessons from fall through spring. Students must provide their own drum sticks. Instructor: Allan Dionne.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details.- Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program.

Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Children 8-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

This program is specifically for beginners (new and learning players) to continue to build on their skills in a fun and inclusive space. In this program everyone plays with all the other beginners as they rotate on and off thru their games.
Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. For all ages programs, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Swimmer 3
description: Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 2. These swimmers will learn how to dive and will do in-water somersaults and handstands to develop weight-transfer skills. They’ll learn Swim to Survive® skills, whip kick on back and will further develop their front crawl and back crawl. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.25 is applicable.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha / Core
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered with an emphasis on the core muscles.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.

title: Ceramics Alternative Firing: Raku
description: Western raku is a low-temperature, fast-firing process for finishing your ceramic sculptures with dazzling effects. Traditional and contemporary raku glazes such as white crackle and metallic copper are provided. Bring 3-4 bisque-fired pieces that can each individually fit within a box measuring 6 inches squared. You may bring additional pieces in case there is extra room in the kiln. Work should be made with a sculpture clay or a grey clay with grog. Glazes included, bring your own brushes. Wear close-toed shoes and wool, cotton or linen long-sleeved clothing. Participants will glaze their work from 10am-12pm, followed by the firing. Participants are responsible for ensuring they have enough work prepared in advance of the firing date. No refunds after November 13. Instructor: Kennedy Snider & Emily SheppardSchedule:Glazing (2 hours) 10am-12pmFiring (4 hours) 12-4pm

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha / Core
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered with an emphasis on the core muscles.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.00.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Reserve in Advance: Basketball All Ages
description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Children 8-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Children 8-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Lunch at Confederation
